text:
Maya: Heads up — we need to trim scope for the Optimize toolkit this sprint. Proposal: ship eval-triggered alerts + lightweight quantization recommendations, defer adaptive batching and persistent KV cache tuning to next sprint. Customers pushing: Acme, NudgeAI, and a pilot at FinWare asking for alerting first.

Aj: Quick context — adaptive batching is infra-heavy (tensor kernels + autoscaler hooks). If we keep alerts + quant recs we can deliver an MVP in ~2 eng-weeks.

Zach: +1 for alerts first. Alerts unlock detection to trigger rollbacks/rollouts and are lower-risk. Quant recs as guidance (non-blocking) should be fine.

Dena: Acceptance criteria suggestion for alerts: 1) webhook delivery <5s median on eval ingest path, 2) false positive rate <10% on our eval suite, 3) docs + runbook. For quant recs: top-3 model/quant combos with estimated cost delta & perf delta.

Maya: Agree. Also we need canary plan: start with internal tenant -> 2 pilot customers -> general availability. Gate: pilot signoff + 2 weeks of stability telemetry.

Aj: Implementation notes — minimal API surface for alerts: 
```http
POST /api/v1/evals/{eval_id}/alerts
{
  "threshold": 0.8,
  "destinations": ["ops","slack:#alerts"],
  "mode": "sampled"
}
```
We can wire to existing webhook dispatcher.

Sam: If we defer batching, we should still leave flags in the codebase so small customers can flip a simple batcher param. Otherwise we risk churn when we pick batching back up.

Zach: Could we scope adaptive batching into "phase 1: heuristics" instead of full runtime changes? I.e., suggestion rules that recommend batch sizes and timeout settings per route. That might be half-sprint and unblock some value.

Maya: I like the heuristics idea as a stretch. Plan: prioritize alerts + quant recs; include heuristics as stretch if no blockers.

Dena: For launch docs: include example alert config, troubleshooting tips, and a short SLOs section. Example alert payload to show customers: 
```json
{
  "eval_id": "eval-2026-03-19-01",
  "metric": "concordance",
  "value": 0.62,
  "threshold": 0.75,
  "samples": ["promptA","promptB"]
}
```

Maya: Dependencies: release-bot deploy window next Wed; need eng signoff by Friday EOD to make it. @Aj can you confirm ETA?

Aj: Confirmed — blockers: 1) small schema change to evals table, 2) webhook retry plumbing (we already have a lib). I can take on schema change, ETA Fri EOD. :thumbsup:

release-bot: Scheduled deploy window: 2026-03-24 02:00-03:00 UTC. Will auto-run smoke tests.

Sam: Customer comms — I'll draft a pilot one-pager that highlights: what triggers an alert, sample remediation steps, and expected noise. Will share by Thurs.

Maya: Risk notes: quant recommendations could cause confusion if we show aggressive quant levels without quality delta. Dena, can you own the expected-quality column for the recs?

Dena: Yep — will produce a simple table: quant level, expected p99 latency delta, expected perplexity delta (or concordance), and recommended workloads.

Zach: Ops ask: include telemetry tags (customer_id, model_version, route) in alert payload for fast triage.

Aj: Will include those tags in payload.

Maya: Decision summary: ship eval-triggered alerts + lightweight quant recs as primary scope. Heuristic batching is stretch. Defer persistent KV cache tuning to next sprint. Gates: pilot signoff + 2 weeks stability telemetry.

Maya: Thanks everyone — I'll update the roadmap doc and product board after this thread.
